title: Introduce regional priority-based degradation policy DSL and runtime enforcement
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a policy DSL and enforcement runtime that enables region-aware, per-customer graceful degradation. Includes emergency unthrottle toggle, metrics instrumentation for SLOs, and console controls.
description:
Context: Production incidents in Jan-Feb exposed two gaps: (1) global load-shedding was too coarse — low-priority customers in healthy regions were shed during remote-region overloads; (2) there was no safe, auditable emergency unthrottle for on-call to selectively re-open capacity during mitigations. This PR introduces a small policy DSL for declaring per-region and per-customer degradation tiers, a runtime evaluator integrated into the front proxy, and a gated emergency unthrottle workflow.

What this changes: 1) policy DSL (pkg/policy/degradation.dsl) — YAML-first, simple predicates (region, customer_tier, route, scope) and actions (shed_rate, downgrade_model_variant, cache_preference). 2) runtime evaluator (proxy/degradation_evaluator.go) — evaluates policies in O(1) for hot paths, caches decisions per-request ID, and respects KV cache hints. 3) emergency unthrottle (ops/unthrottle_api.go + console toggle) — scoped to region and policy id, requires audit headers and an SSO user in the emergency role. 4) metrics and alerts (observability/*) — exposes degraded_request_count, policy_shed_rate, emergency_unthrottle_events for SLO dashboards. 5) tests and docs (tests/integration/degradation_test.go, docs/degradation.md).

Checklist: - [x] DSL spec and parser - [x] Hot-path evaluator with microbenchmarks - [x] Integration with front proxy request path - [x] Emergency unthrottle API + console control with audit logging - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Backwards compatibility notes in docs

Commits summary: - Add DSL grammar and parser (Maya Patel) - Implement evaluator with TTL cache and lock-free reads (Maya Patel) - Wire evaluator into front proxy pre-routing hook (Arjun Mehta) - Add emergency unthrottle API and console integration (Sofia Martinez) - Instrument metrics and add alerts (Ethan Ross) - Tests and docs (Maya Patel)

Files changed (high-level): - pkg/policy/degradation.dsl (new) - pkg/policy/parser.go (new) - proxy/degradation_evaluator.go (modified) - ops/unthrottle_api.go (new) - console/src/components/UnthrottleToggle.tsx (modified) - observability/metrics.yaml (modified) - tests/integration/degradation_test.go (new)

Backward compatibility: DSL defaults to 'no-op' if policy file missing. Existing routes have implicit policy tier 'normal' so this change is opt-in until policies are deployed. No breaking changes expected.

Review thread and decisions: Reviewer (Ethan Ross) requested stronger reasoning about evaluator CPU cost; added microbenchmarks showing <0.6us per decision under contention. Arjun flagged a race between policy reload and cache invalidation; fixed by adding a generation counter and atomic swap of policy pointer plus tests. Sofia requested stricter auditing for emergency unthrottle; added SSO role check and stored reason+operator in audit logs. There was a transient flake in e2e (network timeout on test harness) — CI failed on first run, rerun passed and artifacts uploaded.

CI: initial pipeline: unit tests passed, integration e2e failed (flaky network). Re-run pipeline: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, e2e, load-microbench). Build artifacts: degradation-policy-bundle.tar.gz attached to PR for ops.

Merge: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-22 by Maya Patel after approvals (Ethan, Sofia). Post-merge actions: deployed to staging via canary (perf-canary job) and scheduled for region-by-region rollout with monitoring for policy_shed_rate regressions.

Notes for on-call: - If a region shows elevated policy_shed_rate > 10% for 5m, consider increasing shed_rate thresholds or enabling targeted unthrottle for affected non-critical tenants. - Emergency unthrottle must include incident Jira key in reason; UI blocks submit without either a linked Linear or Jira key.
review_comments: Ethan Ross: Please include microbenchmarks for the evaluator to justify hot-path cost. Also, consider constant-time path for empty-policy case.
Arjun Mehta: Found a race where policy reload could invalidate the cache during reads. Suggest atomic swap pattern and generation counters.
Sofia Martinez: Emergency unthrottle needs stricter auditing; require role check and store operator+reason. Add UI confirmation with incident key.
